clue.text: Feeder, strangely slim, keeps in charge of devotion to the book

parts.note: a bib is worn by a baby while feeding, and also called a feeder

indicators.note: keeps says the scrambled letters hold the next piece inside them
strangely says the letters of slim are put in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A baby's bib, oddly thin, somehow stays in charge of someone's love of reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' and 'keeps' are the two indicators; a bib is also called a feeder because babies wear it to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Biblicism is literal adherence to the Bible, the Book par excellence.

clue.text: Corporation service, a function of weight and height

definitions.text: a function of weight and height

parts.note: a corporation is a body, an organised group of people
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A company's office routine is somehow linked to how heavy and tall someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: Body mass, as in the body mass index, is calculated from a person's weight and height.

clue.text: He's not likely to be a good boy!

definitions.text: He's not likely to be a good boy!

parts.words: He's not likely to be a good boy!
parts.note: a creature unlikely to behave; the words also split as ..., a saint being a good man

explanation.surface: A parent despairs of a naughty son.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BE A ST: the clue says he is unlikely to be a saint (ST), a 'good boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute or wild animal is the opposite of a well-behaved, saintly lad.

clue.text: See 6
He shouldn't be trading in what's said to be drink

indicators.note: said to be marks a word heard rather than written, so the drink's sound is used

parts.note: cider is an apple drink

explanation.surface: A man ought not to be selling while he is in his cups.
explanation.walkthrough: IN plus a word sounding like CIDER gives IN-SIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An insider with confidential knowledge is barred from dealing in shares: insider trading is a crime.

clue.text: 2 award for military junta's problem being contained

indicators.note: being contained says the jumbled letters sit inside the medal abbreviation

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross, a British award for gallantry

indicators.note: problem signals that the letters of junta are in trouble and rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A medal for soldiers is awarded while a military regime's trouble is kept under control.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer of 2 down. 'problem' scrambles the regime's name and 'being contained' sets it inside the medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A muntjac is a small deer, so it is a beast, the answer to 2 down.

clue.text: See humour with bridge system 651 to end game (23 12)

parts.note: lo is an old word for see!, look!
vein can mean mood or humour, as in a jocular vein
Acol is a bidding system in contract bridge
DCLI is 651 in Roman numerals
mate, checkmate, ends a game of chess

explanation.surface: A bridge player's numbered convention finishes the game with a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: '23 12' points at the answers to 23 and 12, together NANCY MITFORD, so the definition is a book by her.
explanation.definitionFit: Nancy Mitford wrote the 1949 novel of this title, sequel to The Pursuit of Love.

clue.text: Antique clocks with a service history?

definitions.meaning: timers that are old, aged timepieces
veterans who served long years, as a used car with a service history has been looked after

explanation.definitionFit: Old timers are aged timekeepers, while old-timers are veterans with long experience.

clue.text: Authenticate a piece of nonsense a little reluctantly

indicators.note: a piece of signals only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone gives a grudging stamp of approval to a bit of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across nonsENSE A Little; 'reluctantly' is surface colour, the approval given grudgingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To enseal is to put a seal on a document, which certifies it as genuine.

clue.text: Variety actors have no answer to ground coffee, about one pound

indicators.note: have no says a stretch is taken away from the word for actors

parts.note: thespians are actors

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go round the next piece
ground coffee is broken up, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Performers with nothing to say grind coffee and pay a pound for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have no' trims the actors' word, 'ground' scrambles the drink, and 'about' wraps it round the pound and one.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says variety is the spice of life, so the phrase stands for variety itself.

clue.text: Doctor of Timothy a help backing wife of Oswald

indicators.note: backing says the whole run of pieces is read from the end to the start

parts.note: taken as written
an is the indefinite article, another form of a
aid means help

explanation.surface: A biblical physician helps out the spouse of a man called Oswald.
explanation.walkthrough: Write DR OF TIM AN AID and read it backwards. Oswald is Sir Oswald Mosley, British fascist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana Mitford married Sir Oswald Mosley in 1936.

clue.text: Summer guards for newspaper with its glasses?

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily newspaper
shades is slang for sunglasses

explanation.surface: Seaside protection from a tabloid paper, complete with its own pair of spectacles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunshades are awnings or parasols that protect from the sun in summer.

clue.text: See 10 and 13
Shakespearean Jewess with German car noted American ends

parts.note: Jessica is Shylock's daughter in The Merchant of Venice
mit is German for with
Ford is a make of car

explanation.surface: Shylock's daughter drives a German car to its noted American end.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: she wrote The American Way of Death, a book on American funerals, so she noted American ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica Mitford, a naturalised American, exposed the US funeral trade in The American Way of Death.

clue.text: Orthodox procedure for music rehearsal?

definitions.meaning: a reliable, correct way of doing things
practice of sound, as musicians rehearse

explanation.definitionFit: Sound practice is good established method; read literally it is practising sounds.

clue.text: Bond's shaken but still in bed?

definitions.meaning: James Bond wants his martini shaken, not stirred
not yet stirred, having not got up

explanation.definitionFit: Unstirred describes Bond's martini and someone who has not yet stirred from sleep.

clue.text: A fellow keeping promises has gift of living

indicators.note: keeping says the word for fellow holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a college
vows are promises

explanation.surface: A college fellow who keeps his word is generous towards the living.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'living' is a Church of England parish post with its income.
explanation.definitionFit: An advowson is the right to appoint the priest to a church benefice, which is called a living.

clue.text: Cool as an owner-occupier?

definitions.meaning: possessed by oneself, as a home owned by its occupant

explanation.definitionFit: Self-possessed means composed and calm; literally it is owned by oneself.

clue.text: Hobby as 23 12's of 6

definitions.meaning: a pastime or interest one follows
Nancy Mitford's novel The ... of Love, 6 being love

explanation.walkthrough: 23 12 is NANCY MITFORD and 6 is LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuit is an activity followed for pleasure, and Mitford's novel is The Pursuit of Love.

clue.text: Quiet walk to the butcher's?

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: Someone strolls softly down to the meat shop.
explanation.walkthrough: A shamble is an old word for a meat stall, as in the Shambles at York.
explanation.definitionFit: A shamble was a butcher's stall or slaughterhouse, the origin of shambles.

clue.text: Arrest by secret policemen

definitions.meaning: a halt or stoppage, as in cardiac arrest
members of the Stasi, East Germany's secret police, taken as a plural

explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a stoppage or standstill, a state of arrest.

clue.text: I'm going to hedge

parts.note: either a tool or gardener about to cut a hedge, or a politician who sits on the fence

explanation.definitionFit: A trimmer cuts hedges, and is also one who shifts opinion to suit, hedging his bets.

clue.text: Name of Spanish king also name of revolutionary

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish monarch's name was also borne by a rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Several kings of Spain were called Alfonso, most recently Alfonso XIII.

clue.text: Pretty boy in French town

definitions.meaning: dated slang for an effeminate young man

explanation.definitionFit: Nancy is an old derogatory term for an effeminate man, and the name of a city in north-east France.

clue.text: Projecting object hurt me badly, making me cry about it

indicators.note: about says the word for cry goes around the jumbled letters

parts.note: to sob is to cry

indicators.note: badly says the letters of hurt me are put in a damaged order

explanation.surface: Someone banged by a sticking-out thing weeps over the injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the two words and 'about' sets the cry around them; 'making me' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that stands out like a sore thumb is conspicuously prominent, as a swollen thumb sticks out.

clue.text: 9's revised by Hammond

indicators.note: revised says the letters are edited into a new order

parts.note: the numeral 9 read as words gives nines

explanation.surface: A cross-reference to answer 9, edited by an author.
explanation.walkthrough: '9's' looks like a reference to 9 down but just means NINES; Hammond Innes was a British thriller writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hammond Innes was the pen name of the novelist Ralph Hammond Innes, so his surname follows Hammond.

clue.text: It could make a splash on the turf first

indicators.note: first says the word for turf comes before the letter that follows

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf

explanation.surface: Something hitting the lawn might cause a splash.
explanation.walkthrough: Whisky with a splash is topped up with soda.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda water is the splash added to a whisky.

clue.text: Historian with time to party and no withdrawing

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

indicators.note: withdrawing means drawing back, so the word for no is read backwards

parts.note: nay means no

explanation.surface: A scholar makes time for a party and refuses to back out.
explanation.walkthrough: G. M. Trevelyan was an English historian.
explanation.definitionFit: G. M. Trevelyan was a celebrated English historian, author of English Social History.
